notes:
I couldn't do this research, so I have no verse-by-verse notes to give you yet.

I tried to fetch six pages in one batch: the Ezekiel 40 pages on enduringword.com, the Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit and Benson commentaries on biblehub.com, and the article on Ezekiel's temple at gotquestions.org. The tool sent back data I couldn't read. While I was trying to inspect it, I hit my limit on web-tool calls for this turn. My other tools can't reach the internet, so I couldn't read any of the pages.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I read nothing, I've left out every point instead of writing notes from memory without real URLs.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll restart the research. I'll fetch one page at a time so a single bad result can't use up my tool calls. The plan:
1. **The traditional reading of each verse:** Enduring Word on Ezekiel 40; the Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit and Benson commentaries on biblehub.com; and Precept Austin.
2. **Differences between Protestant traditions:** Each tradition's own teachers on whether this temple will be literally built in a future age or is a symbol of the church or of God dwelling with his people. Likely sources are gotquestions.org and bible.org for the literal view; ligonier.org, thegospelcoalition.org and monergism.com for the Reformed view; gty.org and desiringgod.org for Baptist views; and wesley.nnu.edu for Wesley's notes.
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes on the measurements and cubits, Bible Odyssey on Ezekiel's temple, and Catholic and Orthodox readings, such as the Church Fathers on the east gate.
